info.title: deAPI REST API
info.description:
Decentralized AI inference API for image generation, video processing, audio transcription, and more.

## Webhooks

Every generation endpoint accepts an optional `webhook_url` (HTTPS only) and an optional
`webhook_secret` (min. 32 chars). We then call you back on each status change instead of you polling.

**Events:** `job.processing`, `job.completed`, `job.failed`.

**Headers we send:** `X-DeAPI-Signature`, `X-DeAPI-Timestamp`, `X-DeAPI-Event`, `X-DeAPI-Delivery-Id`.
Payload and header shapes are documented under `components.schemas`:
`WebhookHeaders`, `WebhookProcessingPayload`, `WebhookCompletedPayload`, `WebhookFailedPayload`.

**Verifying the signature:**

```
X-DeAPI-Signature = "sha256=" + HMAC_SHA256(secret, X-DeAPI-Timestamp + "." + raw_request_body)
```

Hash the **raw** body exactly as received (escaped slashes and all) — re-serializing the parsed JSON
yields a different signature. Reject timestamps older than 5 minutes (replay protection).

**Which secret signs the call:** the per-request `webhook_secret` if you sent one, otherwise your
account-default secret. If neither exists, the call is still delivered but **UNSIGNED** —
`X-DeAPI-Signature` is empty. If you require authenticity, reject an empty signature.

**A per-request `webhook_url` is self-contained:** it is delivered even when your account has no
webhook configuration, or the account webhook is disabled. Failed deliveries are retried
(10 attempts over ~24h).

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Accepted but currently ignored: the page size is fixed at 25 regardless of the value sent. Use `page` to retrieve the remaining results.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number, starting at 1. The response is paginated: a single call returns at most 25 models, so a client that reads only the first page will miss models when `meta.last_page` is greater than 1. Iterate until `meta.current_page` equals `meta.last_page` to obtain the full catalogue.

parameters.name: filter[inference_types]
parameters.description: Comma-separated list of inference types to filter by. Example: txt2img,txt2audio. Values must match the `inference_types` strings returned by this endpoint exactly — note that some of them use hyphens (`img-upscale`, `img-rmbg`, `vid-upscale`, `video-replace`). An unrecognised value is not rejected: the endpoint returns an empty `data` array.

post.description: Unified prompt booster — enhance prompts for any model and type using AI-powered guide system. Accepted `type` values (v2 noun-based dot notation): `images.generations`, `images.edits`, `videos.generations`, `videos.animations`, `audio.speech`, `audio.music`. Only prompt-driven inference types have a booster; upscaling, background removal, OCR, transcription and embeddings are rejected with 422.

WebhookHeaders.title: Webhook Request Headers
WebhookHeaders.description: Headers included in all webhook notification requests. Use these to verify authenticity and process events.

X-DeAPI-Signature.description: HMAC-SHA256 signature for payload verification. Format: sha256=<hex-encoded-hmac>. Calculate as: HMAC-SHA256(key: webhook_secret, message: timestamp + "." + raw_json_payload)

X-DeAPI-Timestamp.description: Unix timestamp when the webhook was sent. Use for replay attack prevention - reject requests older than 5 minutes.

X-DeAPI-Event.description: The type of event that triggered this webhook

X-DeAPI-Delivery-Id.description: Unique identifier for this webhook delivery. Use for idempotency handling.

WebhookProcessingPayload.title: Webhook Payload - Job Processing
WebhookProcessingPayload.description: Payload sent when a job transitions from pending to processing state. Indicates a worker has started processing the job.

timestamp.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the event occurred

job_request_id.description: The UUID of the job request

WebhookCompletedPayload.title: Webhook Payload - Job Completed
WebhookCompletedPayload.description: Payload sent when a job completes successfully. Includes the result URL for downloading the output.

timestamp.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the event occurred

job_request_id.description: The UUID of the job request

completed_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the job completed

result_url.description: URL to download the job result

WebhookFailedPayload.title: Webhook Payload - Job Failed
WebhookFailedPayload.description: Payload sent when a job fails during processing. Includes error details for debugging.

timestamp.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the event occurred

job_request_id.description: The UUID of the job request

failed_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the job failed

error_message.example: Worker failed to respond within the allowed time

error_reason.description: Bounded, actionable failure reason: SOURCE_PRIVATE, SOURCE_RESTRICTED, SOURCE_UNPROCESSABLE, SOURCE_DOWNLOAD_FAILED, INPUT_TOO_LARGE, TIMEOUT, CAPACITY_UNAVAILABLE or PROCESSING_FAILED. THIS LIST IS OPEN — new values may be added without a major version, so treat any unrecognised value as PROCESSING_FAILED. Prefer branching on `retryable`.

retryable.description: Whether resubmitting the identical request could plausibly succeed. Branch on this rather than on error_reason — it stays correct as new reasons are added.

refunded.description: Whether the upfront charge for this job was returned. False covers both a charge deliberately kept and a job that failed before it was ever charged.

source_url.description: URL of video/audio to estimate price for. Mutually exclusive with source_file and duration_seconds. A TikTok URL is only accepted with `model: WhisperLargeV3Ct2` — paired with any other model it is rejected with `422`, exactly as the job would be.

include_ts.description: Should transcription include timestamps. **Required** - send `false` for plain text or `true` for timestamped segments. Whether it raises the quote depends on `ts_level`: segment-level timing is included in the base price. Pass it exactly as you will pass it to POST /api/v2/audio/transcriptions.

ts_level.description: Timestamp granularity. Validated against the model exactly as on POST /api/v2/audio/transcriptions, so a price quote is never returned for a combination the job request would reject. Granularity affects the price on models that price timestamps separately: `segment` is included in the base price, while `word` carries a surcharge.

diarize.description: Label each timed unit with a detected speaker. Requires a model that supports diarization. Implies `include_ts` and carries the timestamp surcharge at ANY granularity, including `segment`.

lang.description: Language hint for the transcription. Does not affect the price, but is validated against the model the same way as on the job request: a language outside a model's published `info.limits.languages` is rejected.

include_metadata.description: Whether the job will be asked to attach source metadata. Carries a flat surcharge on models that price it, so pass it exactly as you will pass it to POST /api/v2/audio/transcriptions or the quote will come in under the amount charged. The surcharge applies only to sources that can actually return metadata: uploads always return null and are never charged for it. Every recognised platform, YouTube included, does return metadata and is charged the surcharge.

metadata.description: Source metadata, present only when the job was submitted with `include_metadata: true`. Null for uploaded files, which have no source to describe. Every field a platform does not expose is null rather than omitted, so the shape is stable across platforms. YouTube resolves through the official Data API and populates only `id`, `title`, `description`, `channel`, `duration_seconds`, `extractor`, `view_count` and `like_count`; the remaining fields are TikTok-only. Some TikTok fields may still be null depending on the individual video.

progress.description: Current progress of the job (0.0 to 100.0)

error_code.description: Category of the failure. Only present when status is error.

error_message.description: A short, stable reason for the failure (e.g. "age-restricted", "context-exceeded", "worker-error"). Only present when status is error.

error_reason.description: Bounded, actionable failure reason. Only present when status is error. SOURCE_PRIVATE: the source is private, deleted or otherwise unavailable to us. SOURCE_RESTRICTED: an age or region gate blocks it. SOURCE_UNPROCESSABLE: the source was fetched but the media is unusable (no audio track, corrupt, unsupported codec). SOURCE_DOWNLOAD_FAILED: the source should be reachable but this attempt failed to fetch it — frequently transient. INPUT_TOO_LARGE: the request exceeds the model limits. TIMEOUT: the job exceeded its time budget. CAPACITY_UNAVAILABLE: our fleet failed to complete it; not your request. PROCESSING_FAILED: ran and failed for a reason we could not classify. THIS LIST IS OPEN — new values may be added without a major version, so treat any value you do not recognise as PROCESSING_FAILED. Prefer branching on `retryable` over matching these individually.

retryable.description: Whether resubmitting the identical request could plausibly succeed. Only present when status is error. Branch on this rather than on `error_reason` — it stays correct as new reasons are added.

refunded.description: Whether the upfront charge for this job was returned. Only present when status is error. False means no refund was issued, which covers both a charge deliberately kept and a job that failed before it was ever charged.

failed_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when the job terminally failed, mirroring the webhook. Only present when status is error.

prompt_boosted.description: Whether the prompt was enhanced by the inline prompt booster (enhance_prompt)

prompt_boost.description: Boosted and original prompts. Non-null only when prompt_boosted is true (i.e. the boost actually ran); null while the boost is still queued or if it was not requested
